title: Acme Freight – pricing and rollout
location: Brightline HQ – Embarcadero room + Google Meet

segments.text: Are they in yet? I don't see anybody in the lobby.
Not yet. It's eleven oh one. Give them a minute.
I'll ping Sarah. She's usually right on time, so.
Hey — before they join. I'm not giving numbers on this call. I want to hear what they need and then put it in writing.
Agreed. No numbers. We listen, we take notes, we come back with something real. Last time we rushed it and it didn't land.
Yeah. Okay. Is the, uh, is the camera pointed at us or at the ceiling?
It's at us. You look great. Oh — there they are.
Okay, I think — can you guys hear us okay? We're in the conference room, so tell me if we sound like we're in a tin can.
You sound fine. A little echoey, but fine.
That's just the room. Embarcadero has, like, zero soft surfaces. It's all glass and a whiteboard nobody uses.
Ha. Ours is the opposite, we're in a room with carpet on the walls. I don't know why. I think it's from the nineties.
It's for acoustics. Allegedly.
Chris, good to see you. How's the week going? You guys in peak yet?
We're getting there. September's always — it starts ramping. The retail stuff starts moving for the holidays and then it's just, you know, go time until January.
Yeah, it's the calm before the storm. Honestly this is a good time to be doing this, because in like six weeks I won't have time to breathe.
Well, we'll try to make it worth it. Thanks for making the time, I know it's — it's a lot of calls this time of year.
No, this one I wanted. This one's actually useful.

We'll take it. So, quick agenda, and tell us if you want to change anything. We wanted to get your read on how things are going on the current version, walk you through what's coming in v2 and how we'd roll it out to your dispatchers, and then talk pricing. Because I know the last proposal didn't quite land.
That's right. Yeah. That works.
And Chris, I know you had some IT questions, so we'll save time for those.
Yeah, I've got a list. It's not long. Well. It's medium.
Okay. Sarah, how's it going? Like, honestly. What are your dispatchers saying?
Um, so, honestly, the dispatchers who use it like it. The route board is way better than what we had before, which was, I mean, it was a whiteboard and a spreadsheet, so the bar was low.

The complaint I get the most is multi-stop. They're still building multi-stop routes kind of by hand, and then dragging stops around, and it takes them — some of the guys at our bigger terminals spend, like, the first two hours of their shift just building routes.
Two hours. Wow. Okay.

And the other thing is the ETAs. The drivers say the ETAs are optimistic. Like, we tell a customer two o'clock and the truck shows up at three fifteen, and then the customer's mad at us, not at the software.
Yeah. Honestly, both of those are basically what v2 is about. Like, that's not me doing a sales thing. That's literally the two things.
It's a little bit a sales thing.
It's a little bit a sales thing. But it's also true.
[laughs] Okay.

So multi-stop optimization is the headline. You give it the stops, the time windows, the vehicle constraints — like which trucks can go where, dock heights, whatever — and it builds the routes. Your dispatchers can still drag things around, but they start from something good instead of from nothing.
Okay. That's — yeah. That's the thing.
Does that run on your side or does it need anything on our side? Like, is there an agent or anything we'd have to install?
All on our side. It's all cloud, nothing to install. The only thing on your side is the driver app, which you already have.
Good. Love that. Every time someone says agent I lose a week.

And on ETAs, we rebuilt how we calculate them. We're using historical route data now, like how long your trucks actually took on that lane at that time of day, instead of just map distance and speed limits. It should get a lot closer. I'm not going to promise perfect.
Nobody's perfect. Just — closer than an hour off would be great.
Can I ask — when the ETA is wrong today, what actually happens? Like, does the dispatcher call the customer?
Usually the customer calls us. Which is the problem.
Yeah.
So if the thing could, like, warn the dispatcher before the customer calls, that alone is — honestly, that's worth a lot to us. That's the thing my CEO would actually notice.

So there's a late-risk flag in v2. It's basic, but it's there. When we think a route's going to miss a delivery window, it turns orange on the board, and you can click into it and see which stop is the problem.
Orange. Okay. Good. Can it text somebody?
Not in v2. It's on the board and it can send an email. Texting is — it's something we've talked about, I just don't want to promise it today.
That's fair. Email's fine to start.
Actually — do you want to just see it? I can share my screen and show you the staging version. It's not final, but it's close.
Yes. Please. That'd be way easier than me imagining it.
Okay, one sec. Can you see my screen? It should be a, a map with a bunch of colored lines.
Yep, we see it.

Okay. So this is the dispatcher board in v2. This is a demo account, so these are fake stops around the Bay Area. On the left you've got all the stops for tomorrow that haven't been assigned yet, and on the right is the map.

So the old way, you'd drag each stop onto a truck. The new way, you hit this button, optimize, and — give it a second — it builds routes for every truck based on the time windows and the truck constraints.
Wait, it did all of them? Just now?
All of them. And each color is a truck. If you click into one — say this blue one — you can see the stop order, the ETA at each stop, and how much slack there is before the window closes.
Okay, that's — yeah. My Stockton people are going to lose their minds. In a good way.
How long does that take with, like, a real fleet? That was a demo with, what, ten trucks?

Twelve trucks here. With a fleet your size it takes longer, it's not instant, it's more like — you'd hit the button and go get a coffee. We're still working on speeding it up for the really big fleets, I'll be honest about that.
A coffee's fine. Two hours is not fine. A coffee's fine.
And then if a dispatcher doesn't like what it did, they can still drag a stop from one truck to another, and it'll re-check the ETAs for both trucks. So they're never locked in.
That's important. My guys hate it when the computer is, like, too sure of itself.
Yeah. The rule we used was, the software suggests, the dispatcher decides.
Can you show me the orange thing? The late one?

Yeah — so here. This truck, the green one, has a stop at the end with a two-to-four window, and it's predicting four-twenty. So the route goes orange, and the stop has this little clock icon. Click it and it tells you why. Here it's, uh, a lot of stops before it and traffic on the bridge.
Okay. Yeah. That's — honestly if I could just have that tomorrow, I'd be happy.
We can do September 30. Tomorrow's a little tight.
[laughs] Fine. Fine.
Okay, I'll stop sharing. Any questions on what you saw?
Is that the same screen on a laptop and on the big wall monitors? Some of our terminals have the board up on a TV on the wall.
Same screen. There's a, a view-only mode for wall displays, it hides the editing stuff and makes the text bigger.
What's the timing on v2? Like, when is this real?
So we just locked the date internally, actually, like yesterday. Route Planner v2 launches September 30.
Oh. That's soon.

It is soon. But we'd roll it out gradually, we're not flipping everybody at once. For you guys I'd suggest we start with one terminal, get those dispatchers comfortable with it, and then expand from there.
That makes sense. We'd probably start with Stockton. They're the most organized. They're also the ones complaining the loudest about multi-stop, so.
Complaining is good. Complaining means they care.
Oh, they care. Trust me. I get a lot of emails.
How many dispatchers are at Stockton?
Stockton's, um, six dispatchers on days and two on nights. And then across all our terminals it's, what, Chris, like forty-something?
Forty-two, I think, last time I pulled the user list. Maybe forty-three with the new guy in Fresno.
Forty-something. Yeah.
Okay. So Stockton would be a nice size for a first wave. Big enough to actually learn something, small enough that if something's weird we can fix it fast.

On the driver app — our drivers are all on the rugged Android devices, and we push apps through our device management. Does the v2 driver app need anything different? Like new permissions or anything?

Good question. I believe it's the same permissions, location and camera for proof of delivery. The update goes through the Play Store like normal, so your device management should just pick it up. But let me double-check that with our engineering lead so I'm not guessing.
Yeah, please. If it asks for a new permission, half the drivers will just hit deny, and then I'm getting calls at five a.m.
Chris, is the location stuff okay with your drivers, generally? Like, we've had some fleets where the drivers were nervous about being tracked.
It was a thing at first. We made it really clear it only tracks when they're on shift, and that helped. As long as that's still true in v2.
That's still true. On-shift only. That's not changing.
Okay, good.
Okay. Should we get into pricing? I feel like that's the —
Yeah, let's do it.

So — let me just be direct, because I think that's easier. The last proposal was per shipment, and I get why you did it that way. But I can't budget that. Our volume swings like crazy. September to December is one thing and then January is, like, a ghost town.
And finance wants a number they can put in a spreadsheet in January and not think about again. Per shipment, they have to, like, forecast our volume just to forecast your bill. And they hate that.

Totally fair. And honestly we've been going back and forth on this internally. Per shipment made sense for some of our smaller customers who have really spiky volume, but for a fleet your size, I think per vehicle is probably a lot cleaner.
Per vehicle is how we think about everything. Fuel, insurance, maintenance, tires, it's all per truck. So if your number is per truck it just — it slots right in.
Right. Yeah. That's kind of what I keep hearing. Fleet ops teams budget by fleet size.
How many vehicles are we talking about? I want to make sure we're sizing this right, because I think the last proposal was working off a pretty old number.
So today we run about 420 vehicles. That's tractors and the straight trucks, all in.
And we expect to be at around 550 by next spring. We're adding a terminal, and we're bringing some of the owner-operator stuff in-house, so the fleet is — it's growing pretty fast.
Okay. So 420 today, around 550 by spring. Got it.
Okay, that's actually really helpful. Because if we price per vehicle, the growth matters a lot. I don't want you to feel like you're getting punished for growing.
Yeah, exactly. That's my fear. If we go to 550 and the bill just goes up in a straight line, my CFO's going to ask me why we're not getting any kind of break for being a bigger customer.
Yeah. Let me take that back. I think there's room to do something smarter as you grow, I just want to actually work through the numbers before I say anything.
Sure. That's fine.
The other thing finance flagged was the onboarding fee. Is that — would that still be in there?
Let me take that back too. I don't want to say something on a call and then walk it back in writing.
What I'll say is we want you guys long-term. We'd rather structure it as, you know, a multi-year thing that works for both sides than nickel-and-dime you on setup.
Multi-year is probably fine. We'd want some kind of out if it's really not working, but in principle multi-year is fine. We did three years with our telematics provider.
And just so I understand your side — per vehicle, is that per vehicle per month, or do you think about it annually?
Per month is easier for me to compare, honestly. Everything else I look at is monthly. Finance will annualize it anyway.
Okay. Per vehicle per month. Got it.
And do you count vehicles that are, like, in the shop? Or seasonal trucks you park in January?
Ooh. Good question. I mean — I'd want to only pay for the ones that are actually running, but I know that's a pain.
Yeah, we'd probably count active vehicles on the account, like trucks that ran a route that month. I'll think about how to make that clean.
That would be great, honestly. January would thank you.
And timing on your side — like, what does your approval process look like for something like this? Who has to sign off?
So it'd go to me, then our CFO, and then if it's over a certain amount it goes to our CEO too, which it probably is. It's not — it's not fast, but it's not terrible.
Hi, sorry, jumping on late. [inaudible]
Hey, no worries. We were just talking about pricing and, uh, timing on your side.
Yeah. We're just getting to the approval piece.
So you were saying CFO and then probably CEO. Is there a, like, a time of year that's better or worse for that?
Just so you know, our fiscal year ends in November, so anything needing budget approval has to land before then.
Yeah — right. That's a good point. After November it basically goes into next year's budget and that's a whole other process.
Okay, that's really helpful. So we want the paperwork in front of you well before November. Noted.
Noted. Very noted.
It's not a hard wall, it's just — it's a lot easier if it's in this year's numbers.
Makes sense. We'll work backwards from that.
Can I jump in with the IT stuff while we're on the contract-ish topics?
Yeah, please. Go for it.
Okay. So first, data. If we ever leave — not that we're planning to — can we get our data out? Routes, stops, delivery history, all of it.
Yes. There's a CSV export in the app for most of it, and everything's available through the API. And if you ever leave, we'd do a full export for you. It's your data.
Okay, good. In a format that's not, like, a proprietary blob?
CSV and JSON. No blobs.
Great. Second — user management. Right now when we add a dispatcher, someone on Sarah's team has to go invite them by email, right?
Yeah, it's me. It's usually me. At eleven p.m.
Oh — and that's actually the thing I wanted to ask, and Chris is going to kill me if I don't. SSO. Do you guys support SSO? Like single sign-on with our identity provider?
Yeah, we're on octa. Everything new we roll out has to go through Okta now. It's kind of a hard rule for us since last year.
Yeah. So today, no — today it's email and password with two-factor. But SSO is on our Q4 roadmap.
Q4. Okay. So, like, by the end of the year?
That's the plan, yeah.
Is it sample or OIDC? Like, which protocol?
SAML first, I'd think. I'd have to check with the team on the exact details, but SAML with Okta is the obvious one to start with, because that's what everybody asks for.
Okay. And provisioning — like, if someone leaves, do they get turned off automatically? SCIM or whatever?
That one I genuinely don't know. Let me find out. I'd rather tell you I don't know than make something up.
Appreciate that. Honestly. You'd be surprised how many vendors just say yes to everything.
For the pilot terminal I can live with email and password. But for the full rollout, forty-plus dispatchers, I'd need SSO. I can't have forty passwords floating around.
Okay, so that kind of works, right? If we start with Stockton this fall, and SSO comes in Q4, then by the time we go wide, it's there.
Yeah, that lines up nicely.
Okay. Third thing. Do you have some kind of security overview? Like how data's handled, encryption, where it's hosted. Our security review needs something in writing.
Yep, we've got a security overview doc. I'll send it to you after this.
Great, thanks. That's — that's actually most of my list. I said medium.

Oh, one more from me. Integration. Right now our dispatchers are looking at your app and our telematics dashboard side by side. Is there any way to get the truck locations from our telematics into your board, instead of from the driver app?
Maybe. Which provider are you on?
Chris?
I'll send it over. We're on one of the big ones. They have an API, it's — it's decent.
Okay. We have a couple of telematics integrations already and a couple more on the list. Send me the name and I'll tell you honestly where it is. It's not in v2 at launch, I can tell you that.
That's fine. That's a nice-to-have. Multi-stop and the ETAs are the must-haves.
Good. Because those we can do.
Sarah, can I ask — for the Stockton pilot, what would success look like for you? Like, what would you need to see to say, okay, let's roll this out everywhere?
Um. Honestly? If route building goes from two hours to, like, thirty minutes, that alone. And if we get fewer angry calls about late trucks. I don't have a number on that, but my team would feel it.
Can we measure the route-building time before and after? Like, actually time it for a week before they switch?
Yeah, I can have the terminal manager track it. That's easy. They already complain about it, might as well count it.
What's your support like? Our dispatchers start at four in the morning. If something breaks at four fifteen, who do they call?

Support is email and in-app chat, and we have on-call engineering for anything that's actually down. Early mornings — honestly, human coverage at four a.m. Pacific is thin today. Let me get you a real answer on that instead of a hand-wavy one.
Okay. That's fair. It matters for us though, four a.m. is when everything happens.
That's a good flag. We'll come back on it.
Do you have other customers our size we could talk to? Like, a reference? My CFO is going to ask.
Yeah, absolutely. I'll line one up. There's a couple of fleets in the same range who'd be happy to talk.
Great. Someone who's actually used the multi-stop stuff would be ideal, but I know it's new.
Right, it's new. But I'll find someone who's been in the beta, at least.
Sarah, is there anything else on your side that's a must-have we haven't talked about? Like, anything that would stop you from signing?
Um. Pricing that my CFO can live with. SSO before we go wide. And honestly just that it works. Like, that Stockton doesn't hate it.
If Stockton hates it, I will hear about it for a year.
Then we'll make sure Stockton doesn't hate it.
We could — Alex, maybe we do a session with the Stockton dispatchers once they're on it? Like a check-in a couple weeks in.
Yeah, I'd love that. I'd actually love to just watch them use it for an hour. Honestly that's the most useful thing I can do.
They'd love that. They'd tell you everything. Bring snacks.
[crosstalk] — donuts, they like donuts, right?
Everybody likes donuts, Marcus.
Okay. We're coming up on time, so let's just do next steps.
Yeah. So, from our side. I'll send you the revised pricing proposal by Friday. Per vehicle, per month, and I'll take a real look at how we handle the growth to 550, and at the onboarding fee.
Friday's great. Send it to me directly and I'll get it in front of our CFO.
Will do. And I'll find out about the driver app permissions and the provisioning question for Chris.
And I'll send Chris the security overview today, and once you've had a chance to look at the proposal I'll set up a follow-up with everybody.
Sounds good. And I'll send over the telematics details.
And on our side we'll figure out who from Stockton should be in the first group. I'll talk to their terminal manager this week.
Thanks, everyone. I'm going to drop. [inaudible]
Thanks. Okay — thank you all, seriously. This was really useful.
Thanks, Alex. Thanks, Marcus. Talk soon.
Thanks, guys.
Bye, everybody.
Okay. I think that went well. That went really well, actually.
Yeah. She's — Sarah's great. She just tells you what she needs.
Hey, did you catch who that was that joined late? The person who said the fiscal year thing?
No idea. I figured you knew. I didn't see a name, it just said, like, a phone number or something.
Huh. Okay. Well, it's good to know regardless. November.
Yeah, that actually matters. If this slips past November, we're in next year's budget, and that's a whole other cycle. Let's not let it slip.
Agreed. Okay, I've got to get the proposal done by Friday. Can we grab thirty minutes tomorrow to go through numbers?
Yeah, I'll throw something on your calendar. Nice job.
You too. Okay, stopping this.
